source: Orientation video for the Trinity tab (ev-s6). Arguments from the certified ev-s6 essays (shema, nt_trinity, ot_trinity, jesus_as_god_nt, holy_spirit, early_church_trinity, philosophical_trinity, analogies, modalism, trinity_islam/jw/mormons, etc.). DOCTRINE: one God, three co-equal co-eternal persons — NEVER modalism ('one person in three masks') or tritheism ('three gods'); persons distinct, essence one. NO diagram (owner ruling). 'makes the case', never 'proves'.
voiceover: One God, eternally three persons. Is that a contradiction the church invented — or the truth the evidence of Scripture points to? This section makes the case. It starts where Israel starts — there is one God, and only one. The Trinity never adds a second; that oneness is non-negotiable. Yet the New Testament gives to the Son and to the Spirit what belongs to God alone — the divine name, the divine works, and worship. This was not voted into being at Nicaea. The earliest Christians already prayed to Jesus and lived as though Father, Son, and Spirit were each fully God. It is not one person wearing three masks, and it is not three gods — the persons are distinct, the essence one. And the section answers the Muslim, the Jehovah's Witness, and the Mormon on their own terms. Every one of these arguments gets a fully-cited deep-dive essay. Each claim is sourced, and the strongest objections are stated fairly, then answered. That is our standard — Checked Before Published. And you will not just read. On every essay an AI tutor answers your questions — ask it anything, or highlight a single sentence and ask about that exact line. Mastery mode lets you explain the argument back in your own words and have it graded. Daily practice brings the key points back just as you are about to forget them. There are pocket cards to share, and a Debate Arena to practise against an AI sceptic before the real conversation. Every essay comes in a plain-English version and a full deep dive, with read-aloud audio. The Trinity is beyond full comprehension, but it is not a contradiction. What this section makes the case for is that it is exactly where the evidence of Scripture points — and that it holds together. Start anywhere, and follow it where it leads.
